result.version_source: gh api https://api.github.com/repos/Aider-AI/aider/releases/latest -> tag v0.86.0 (published 2025-08-09); PyPI JSON https://pypi.org/pypi/aider-chat/json -> 0.86.2 (docs evidence read from aider.chat, main branch)

features.note: No sub-agent/child-agent concept in v0.86 docs or code; architect mode's two LLM roles are a fixed pipeline, not spawnable agents.
Only multi-model construct is architect/editor, a single fixed two-role pipeline; no DAGs, teams, swarms, or orchestration scripting.
No MCP client or server support: zero mentions of MCP anywhere in v0.86 docs or code, and no MCP flags or config.
No lifecycle hook API; closest are default-on auto-lint/auto-test after edits and --notifications-command. Only 'hooks' option is a git pre-commit --no-verify toggle.
No skill/prompt-pack registry; closest is a CONVENTIONS.md markdown file (or --read files) added to chat as static prompt context.

features.evidence_quote: Specify the chat history file (default: .aider.chat.history.md)
features.note: Per-project chat transcript persisted to disk and reloadable; no structured long-term memory store.

features.evidence_quote: Always say yes to every confirmation
features.note: Shell commands and edits to unadded files require explicit y/n approval by default (code-verified); --yes-always/dry-run bypass. No OS sandbox or graded permission modes.

features.evidence_quote: Use ask mode to discuss what you want to do, get suggestions or options from aider
features.note: Ask/architect modes support plan-then-execute ('go ahead' in code mode) but there is no plan artifact or approval gate.
No background/async task execution; --watch-files is a foreground watcher for 'AI!' code comments.
No official VS Code/JetBrains extension; 'Aider in your IDE' means watch mode reacting to AI comments from any editor, run alongside the terminal.

features.evidence_quote: Aider can connect to most LLMs for AI pair programming.
features.note: Docs cover OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, DeepSeek, xAI, OpenRouter, Azure, Bedrock, Groq, local Ollama/LM Studio, and OpenAI-compatible endpoints.
No plugin or extension API in docs or code; third parties can only wrap the CLI externally.

features.evidence_quote: Restore the previous chat history messages (default: False)
features.note: --restore-chat-history reloads the project's last transcript (.aider.chat.history.md) into the LLM conversation (code-verified); no multi-session picker.

features.evidence_quote: Report on the number of tokens used by the current chat context
features.note: /tokens reports context tokens; aider also prints per-message and session dollar cost after each reply (code-verified).

result.promises: Aider is "AI Pair Programming in Your Terminal": it lets you pair program with LLMs to start a new project or build on your existing codebase, with AI changes automatically committed using sensible git commit messages.
result.surprises: Despite huge popularity, v0.86 ships no MCP, plugin, subagent, or lifecycle-hook support, and the GitHub "latest release" (v0.86.0) lags the PyPI version users actually install (0.86.2).

features.evidence_quote: Subagents are specialized AI assistants that handle specific types of tasks.
features.note: Claude delegates matching tasks to a subagent that works independently in its own context and returns results; supports foreground/background runs and persistent memory.

features.evidence_quote: Dynamic workflows orchestrate many subagents from a script Claude writes and you can rerun.
features.note: JS scripts run in background; agent teams exist too but are experimental and disabled by default (CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1).

features.evidence_quote: Claude Code can connect to hundreds of external tools and data sources through the Model Context Protocol (MCP), an open source standard for AI-tool integrations.
features.note: Client for MCP servers; also acts as an MCP server for other apps via `claude mcp serve`.

features.evidence_quote: Hooks are user-defined shell commands, HTTP endpoints, MCP tool calls, LLM prompts, or subagents that execute automatically at specific points in Claude Code's lifecycle.
features.note: Lifecycle events include SessionStart/SessionEnd, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse/PostToolUse, Stop/StopFailure.

features.evidence_quote: Skills extend what Claude can do. Create a SKILL.md file with instructions, and Claude adds it to its toolkit.
features.note: Follows the Agent Skills open standard; Claude invokes automatically when relevant or directly via /skill-name.

features.evidence_quote: Auto memory lets Claude accumulate knowledge across sessions without you writing anything.
features.note: Two mechanisms: user-written CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md files plus self-written auto memory, both loaded at session start.

features.evidence_quote: The Bash sandbox is a boundary that the operating system enforces around the shell commands Claude runs on your machine.
features.note: Off by default (`/sandbox`); macOS/Linux/WSL2 only (native Windows unsandboxed); permission modes (default/acceptEdits/plan/auto/bypassPermissions) add approval control.

features.evidence_quote: Plan mode tells Claude to research and propose changes without making them. Claude reads files, runs shell commands to explore, and writes a plan
features.note: Edits stay blocked until the user approves the plan; `claude --permission-mode plan` or Shift+Tab cycle.

features.evidence_quote: Claude Code supports running Bash commands in the background, allowing you to continue working while long-running processes execute.
features.note: Ctrl+B backgrounds bash/agents; /tasks shows running shells and subagents; workflows also execute in background.

features.evidence_quote: Use Claude Code with JetBrains IDEs including IntelliJ, PyCharm, WebStorm, and more
features.note: VS Code extension too (inline diffs, @-mentions, plan review, resume past conversations), per docs index and vs-code page.

features.evidence_quote: If you deploy through Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry, or Claude Platform on AWS
features.note: Multiple cloud providers and LLM gateways supported, but all serve Anthropic's Claude models only — no non-Anthropic LLMs (no GPT/Gemini).

features.evidence_quote: A Claude Code plugin is a directory of skills, agents, hooks, MCP servers, or other components that Claude Code installs and loads as one unit.
features.note: Distributed via marketplaces; install with /plugin (Discover tab); users can also build and publish their own.

features.evidence_quote: A session is a saved conversation tied to a project directory. Claude Code stores it locally as you work
features.note: `claude --continue`, `claude --resume` (picker or named), `/resume`, `--from-pr`; transcripts stored locally as .jsonl.

features.evidence_quote: The Session block at the top of `/usage` shows detailed token usage statistics for your current session.
features.note: /usage command, team spend limits, org-wide usage monitoring (monitoring-usage page), model selection and context management to reduce cost.

result.promises: An agentic coding tool that lives in your terminal, understands your codebase, and helps you code faster by executing routine tasks, explaining complex code, and handling git workflows — all through natural language commands. It reads your codebase, edits files, runs commands, and integrates with your development tools across terminal, IDE, desktop app, and browser. (README + docs overview.)
result.surprises: Despite the multi-agent story, agent teams are experimental and off by default (CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1), and since v2.1.283 the default interactive permission mode is "auto", where a second classifier model — not the user — reviews actions.

Concurrent trains in same repo: VS Code/JetBrains extension v4.1.22, CLI cli-v3.0.68 (npm cline@3.0.68), SDK sdk/sdk/v0.0.90.

features.evidence_quote: Subagents let Cline spawn focused research agents that run in parallel.
features.note: Experimental; read-only (cannot edit, use MCP, or nest), own context/token budget; enabled by default across VS Code, JetBrains, CLI; per-subagent cost tracked.

features.evidence_quote: Agent teams let you break complex work across multiple agents that coordinate through a shared task board.
features.note: Coordinator/teammate tools (spawn, delegate, status, result) via SDK team_spawn_teammate; persistent team state; Kanban worktrees + dependency chains. Warning on page: not applicable to VS Code/JetBrains extension for now.

features.evidence_quote: MCP (Model Context Protocol) lets Cline use external tools and data sources through MCP servers.
features.note: Client-side: local STDIO + remote Streamable HTTP/SSE, .cline/mcp.json, CLI wizard (`cline mcp`), autoApprove allowlists, enterprise allowlisting. No Cline-as-MCP-server mode documented.

features.evidence_quote: The available lifecycle hooks are `beforeRun`, `afterRun`, `beforeModel`, `afterModel`, `beforeTool`, `afterTool`, and `onEvent`.
features.note: Stages include session_start, tool_call_before/after, run_end, session_shutdown; CLI flags --hooks-dir and `cline hook`. Scoped to SDK/CLI/Kanban; extension hooks doc is a stub pointing at SDK plugins.

features.evidence_quote: Skills are modular instruction sets that extend Cline's capabilities for specific tasks.
features.note: SKILL.md + YAML frontmatter with progressive loading (metadata ~100 tokens); activated by description match via use_skill tool or explicit slash command; subagents can load skills.

features.evidence_quote: Through structured markdown files, Cline can "remember" your project details across sessions.
features.note: Official Memory Bank methodology: markdown files in-repo wired via .clinerules custom instructions; document-driven rather than automatic. Session/task history and checkpoints also persist.

features.evidence_quote: Auto Approve lets you decide which actions Cline can take without prompting you each time.
features.note: Per-tool-category permission modes (read/edit/commands/browser/MCP) plus YOLO mode; CLI adds CLINE_SANDBOX env and CLINE_COMMAND_PERMISSIONS allow/deny glob policy. OS-level sandbox details not documented.

features.evidence_quote: Plan & Act modes separate thinking from doing. Plan mode lets you explore and strategize without changing files.
features.note: Plan mode read-only, Act executes; conversation carries over on switch; CLI -p/--plan flag; ACP clients get mode selector.

features.evidence_quote: For long-running processes like dev servers, Cline continues working in the background and reacts to new output as it appears
features.note: Background terminal output monitoring; CLI -z/--zen starts session in background hub daemon; cron-scheduled agents persist across restarts (schedule docs scoped to SDK/CLI/Kanban).

features.evidence_quote: Cline works across all major editors: VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf, JetBrains (IntelliJ, PyCharm, WebStorm), Antigravity, and Zed, Neovim via ACP mode.
features.note: VS Code/Cursor/Windsurf extension, JetBrains plugin, ACP mode for Zed/Neovim/Emacs, plus CLI/TUI and Desktop app surfaces.

features.evidence_quote: Cline is not locked to a single AI provider. Use whichever model fits your workflow:
features.note: BYOK cloud and local (Ollama/LM Studio); docs list 40+ providers: Anthropic, OpenAI/Codex, Gemini, OpenRouter (200+ models), Bedrock, Vertex, Cerebras, Groq, Qwen, DeepSeek, Z AI and an 'Other 30+ Providers' page.

features.evidence_quote: Plugins extend Cline with custom tools, lifecycle hooks, slash commands, and more.
features.note: AgentPlugin API; `cline plugin install` from npm, git, file URL, or local path; global (~/.cline/plugins) or project scope; reference typescript-lsp-plugin. Warning on page: applies to SDK/CLI/Kanban only, not VS Code/JetBrains extension for now.

features.evidence_quote: Resume an existing session by ID
features.note: CLI --id resumes a session; `cline history` lists/manages saved sessions; ACP persists conversations so clients restore threads after restart; team state persists across sessions.

features.evidence_quote: Subagent costs (tokens and API spend) are tracked separately per subagent and rolled into the total cost.
features.note: UI shows per-subagent and task token/cost; token usage visible in task header; SDK getAccumulatedUsage(sessionId); production guide shows abort-on-cost-limit pattern; schedule history and enterprise show tokens/cost.

result.promises: Open source coding agent that lives in your IDE, terminal, and desktop: it reads files, writes code, and runs commands. Its pitch stresses control — every action requires your explicit approval, so you stay in charge.
result.surprises: Far beyond its VS Code-extensions origin, Cline now ships an SDK with a hub-spoke background daemon, CLI, desktop app, and a Kanban multi-agent board — yet agent teams, plugins, hooks, and scheduling are explicitly 'not applicable on VSCode and JetBrains Extension for now', and GitHub's 'latest release' is desktop-v0.0.43 while the extension train sits at v4.1.22.

result.docs_home: https://developers.openai.com/codex (redirects to https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs; per-page markdown at <url>.md)

features.evidence_quote: ChatGPT Work and Codex can run subagent workflows by spawning specialized agents in parallel and then collecting their results in one response.
features.note: Enabled by default in current Codex releases; /agent inspects and switches between running threads; custom agents definable with own model and instructions.

features.evidence_quote: ChatGPT or Codex handles orchestration across agents, including spawning new subagents, routing follow-up instructions, waiting for results, and closing agent threads.
features.note: config-reference lists primitives spawn_agent, send_input, resume_agent, wait_agent, close_agent (features.multi_agent, stable, on by default); concurrent-thread caps configurable.

features.evidence_quote: Local Codex clients can also connect directly to MCP servers and share their configuration.
features.note: Client only: STDIO + Streamable HTTP, OAuth login, tool allow/deny lists via codex mcp add/list/login; the codex mcp-server binary was removed (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/mcp-server.md).

features.evidence_quote: Hooks are an extensibility framework for Codex. They let you run scripts or MCP tools during the agentic loop
features.note: Events: PreToolUse, PermissionRequest, PostToolUse, PreCompact, PostCompact, UserPromptSubmit, SubagentStart/Stop, Stop, SessionStart/SessionEnd, Interrupt; command hooks can run async in background.

features.evidence_quote: A skill is a directory with a `SKILL.md` file plus optional scripts and references.
features.note: Progressive disclosure; invoked as $skill-name or /skills; read from repository (.agents/skills), user, admin, and system locations; skills can ship inside plugins.

features.evidence_quote: Memories let ChatGPT and Codex carry useful context from earlier work into future work.
features.note: Local Codex memories are off by default; local memory store under Codex home; enable via [features] memories = true.

features.evidence_quote: The sandbox defines which files and network resources ChatGPT can access.
features.note: Sandbox modes read-only | workspace-write | danger-full-access plus approval policies; hooks expose current permission_mode (default, acceptEdits, plan, dontAsk, bypassPermissions).

features.evidence_quote: Ask Codex to propose an execution plan before implementation work starts.
features.note: /plan switches to plan mode and optionally sends a prompt; plan_mode_reasoning_effort config; plan is also a permission_mode value in hooks.

features.evidence_quote: Show background terminals and their recent output.
features.note: /ps and /stop manage background terminals; background_terminal_max_timeout config (default 300000 ms) controls background terminal polling; async hook handlers run in background.

features.evidence_quote: VS Code and compatible editors use the Codex extension; Xcode and JetBrains IDEs provide their own integrations.
features.note: Also Cursor, Windsurf, VS Code Insiders; the IDE extension does not support plugins.

features.evidence_quote: Built-in provider IDs (`openai`, `ollama`, and `lmstudio`) are reserved and cannot be overridden.
features.note: Custom model_providers.<id> with base_url; --oss flag with oss_provider for local models; docs cover Amazon Bedrock and LLM gateways.

features.evidence_quote: Plugins bundle capabilities into reusable workflows in ChatGPT and Codex. They can include skills and MCP servers.
features.note: Codex CLI has a /plugins browser to install from a configured marketplace; IDE extension doesn't support plugins.

features.evidence_quote: Reopen a recent chat from the current repository, or search across local chats when you need to return to older work.
features.note: Via `codex resume`; hooks SessionStart matcher includes resume.

features.evidence_quote: Display session configuration and token usage.
features.note: /status shows session token usage and remaining context; /usage shows account token activity and rate-limit resets; rollout_budget token-limit feature exists but is experimental and off by default.

result.promises: Codex CLI is a coding agent from OpenAI that runs locally on your computer (repo README). It promises to let you inspect code, make changes, run commands, and automate repeatable work without leaving your terminal, staying in control of model, reasoning effort, and permissions.
result.surprises: Far beyond the "local coding agent" pitch: current releases ship subagents on by default, lifecycle hooks, skills, a plugin browser, local memories, and plan/goal modes — yet OpenAI removed the codex mcp-server binary, so Codex consumes MCP but no longer acts as an MCP server.

result.version_source: gh api repos/google-gemini/gemini-cli/releases/latest -> tag v0.62.0, https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/releases/tag/v0.62.0 (published 2026-09-29); cross-checked npm @google/gemini-cli@0.62.0 via https://registry.npmjs.org/@google/gemini-cli/latest

features.evidence_quote: Subagents are "specialists" that the main Gemini agent can hire for a specific job.
features.note: Built-in codebase_investigator plus custom, extension-bundled, and remote (A2A) agents; automatic delegation, @name forcing, /agents list|enable|disable; each runs in its own context loop to save main-context tokens.

features.evidence_quote: Gemini CLI supports connecting to remote subagents using the Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol.
features.note: Multi-agent delegation primitives exist (local subagents, A2A remote agents, extension-bundled agents, headless scripting + an experimental a2a-server package), but no DAG/team/swarm orchestration layer.

features.evidence_quote: An MCP server is an application that exposes tools and resources to the Gemini CLI through the Model Context Protocol
features.note: MCP client over Stdio, SSE, and Streamable HTTP with tool and resource discovery; extensions can bundle MCP servers. No documented MCP-server mode for Gemini CLI itself.

features.evidence_quote: Hooks are scripts or programs that Gemini CLI executes at specific points in the agentic loop, allowing you to intercept and customize behavior
features.note: 11 events including SessionStart, SessionEnd, BeforeAgent/AfterAgent, BeforeTool/AfterTool, BeforeModel/AfterModel; hooks can block tools, rewrite args, and inject context.

features.evidence_quote: Agent Skills let you extend Gemini CLI with specialized expertise, procedural workflows, and task-specific resources.
features.note: Implements the agentskills.io open standard; SKILL.md directories discovered from built-in, extension, user, and workspace tiers; activate_skill tool with user consent, plus /skills command.

features.evidence_quote: Instead of repeating instructions in every prompt, you can define them once in a context file.
features.note: Hierarchical GEMINI.md (global, workspace/parent, just-in-time) with @file.md imports (memport); experimental Auto Memory mines past session transcripts into reviewable memory patches and skill drafts.

features.evidence_quote: Sandboxing isolates potentially dangerous operations (such as shell commands or file modifications) from your host system
features.note: Docker/Podman/macOS seatbelt containers via -s flag, GEMINI_SANDBOX env, or settings.json; backed by approval modes (default/auto-edit/plan/YOLO) and a policy engine for tool permissions.

features.evidence_quote: Plan Mode is a read-only environment for architecting robust solutions before implementation.
features.note: Enter via --approval-mode=plan, /plan [goal], Shift+Tab cycle, or natural language; agent researches read-only, agrees strategy with ask_user, writes a Markdown plan for approval before executing.

features.evidence_quote: is_background (boolean, optional): Whether to move the process to the background immediately after starting.
features.note: run_shell_command can background processes and returns Background PIDs, with a BackgroundTaskDisplay UI (confirmed by repo paths packages/cli/src/ui/components/BackgroundTaskDisplay.tsx and evals/background_processes.eval.ts); no generic async agent-task queue documented.

features.evidence_quote: The Gemini CLI Companion extension grants Gemini CLI direct access to your VS Code compatible IDEs
features.note: VS Code companion (open files, cursor, selection context, native diffing, command palette) plus ACP mode (--acp / --experimental-acp) used for JetBrains and Zed via the ACP Agent Registry.

features.evidence_quote: Local model routing uses a local Gemma 3 1B model running on your machine to classify and route user requests.
features.note: Generation is Gemini-only: /model lists just gemini-3-pro/flash-preview and gemini-2.5-pro/flash across Google account, Gemini API key, or Vertex AI auth. The one local-model feature (Gemma) is Google's own and used only for routing decisions; no OpenAI/Anthropic/other providers documented.

features.evidence_quote: Gemini CLI extensions package prompts, MCP servers, custom commands, themes, hooks, sub-agents, and agent skills into a familiar and user-friendly format.
features.note: Install from GitHub URLs or local paths; manage via /extensions and gemini extensions commands; official extension gallery (geminicli.com/extensions/browse) with publishing docs for third parties.

features.evidence_quote: You can resume a previous session to continue the conversation with all prior context restored.
features.note: gemini --resume/-r [latest|index] and interactive session browser; sessions auto-saved per project under ~/.gemini/tmp. Also /rewind (chat and/or code revert) and optional checkpointing with /restore.

features.evidence_quote: Show model-specific usage statistics, including token counts and quota information.
features.note: /stats session|model|tools reports tokens, duration, and quota; OpenTelemetry telemetry exports usage metrics; documented per-auth-method quota tiers (1,000-2,000 requests/day etc.). No hard spend-cap/limit setting documented.

result.promises: An open-source AI agent that brings Gemini models directly into your terminal - "giving you the most direct path from your prompt to our model" - with built-in tools (Google Search grounding, file ops, shell, web fetch) and MCP extensibility. Promises a free tier of 60 requests/min and 1,000 requests/day with a personal Google account, plus Gemini 3 models with a 1M-token context window.
result.surprises: The official docs banner and Google Developers Blog announce that Gemini CLI was replaced by Antigravity CLI on June 18, 2026 for free, Pro, and Ultra users, yet the repo keeps shipping weekly releases (v0.62.0, Sep 29, 2026) for enterprise and API-key users - a live-but-transitioning project.

features.evidence_quote: Subagents are independent instances that execute tasks while keeping your main conversation clean and focused.

features.evidence_quote: Different subrecipes run one after another unless explicitly requested to run in parallel

features.evidence_quote: Connect to 70+ extensions via the Model Context Protocol open standard.

features.evidence_quote: Hooks let you run your own scripts when key events happen during a goose session.

features.evidence_quote: Skills are reusable sets of instructions and resources that teach goose how to perform specific tasks.

features.evidence_quote: goose loads all saved memories at the start of a session and includes them in every prompt sent to the LLM.

features.evidence_quote: Smart Approval — Automatically approves low-risk actions and flags others for approval.

features.evidence_quote: The CLI `/plan` command described in this post has since been removed from goose

features.evidence_quote: Automate goose recipes by scheduling them to run with a cron expression.

features.evidence_quote: The goose for VS Code extension connects directly to your editor, letting you manage files, projects, and workflows with AI.

features.evidence_quote: goose works with 15+ providers — Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Ollama, OpenRouter, Azure, Bedrock, and more.

features.evidence_quote: A plugin is the container. Skills and hooks are components inside that container.

features.evidence_quote: -r, --resume: Resume a previous session

result.promises: Goose promises a general-purpose AI agent that "runs on your machine" — "Not just for code" but research, writing, automation, and data analysis, extensible via 70+ MCP extensions and working with 15+ model providers.

features.evidence_quote: Use this to run multiple units of work in parallel.

features.evidence_quote: OpenCode uses the AI SDK and Models.dev to support 75+ LLM providers and it supports running local models.

features.evidence_quote: Continue the last session

features.evidence_quote: Show token usage and cost statistics for your OpenCode sessions.
features.note: opencode stats with --days/--models breakdown; --verbose shows cost metadata; per-agent 'steps' cap limits agentic iterations to control cost; Zen pay-as-you-go pricing.

result.promises: An open source AI coding agent ("The open source AI coding agent") available as a terminal TUI, desktop app, or IDE extension, usable with any of 75+ LLM providers including local models. It promises a plan-first workflow (read-only Plan agent) with full-access Build agent, undo/redo, shareable sessions, and Claude Code-compatible AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md conventions.
result.surprises: Deep Claude Code compatibility is a first-class fallback path (reads CLAUDE.md and .claude/skills unless disabled), plus a /oc GitHub bot that runs entire tasks inside your repo's GitHub Actions runners.

result.repo: All-Hands-AI/OpenHands (repo now redirects to OpenHands/OpenHands after org rename)

features.evidence_quote: The TaskToolSet lets a parent agent launch sub-agents that handle complex, multi-step tasks autonomously.
features.note: SDK-level TaskToolSet: parent spawns typed sub-agents (register_agent), runs sequentially, resumable via task_id; file-based sub-agents can be plain Markdown.

features.evidence_quote: The TaskManager creates (or resumes) a sub-agent conversation, runs it to completion, and returns the result to the parent.
features.note: Has sub-agent delegation (sequential, blocking), scheduled/event automations, and GitHub Actions workflow templates; no DAG/team/swarm orchestration primitives documented.

features.evidence_quote: Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard that allows OpenHands to communicate with external tool servers, extending the agent's capabilities with custom tools
features.note: MCP client; SSE/SHTTP/stdio transports; full support on CLI, SDK, Local GUI and Cloud.

features.evidence_quote: Hooks let you run custom shell scripts at key moments during an OpenHands session.
features.note: PreToolUse, PostToolUse, UserPromptSubmit, Stop, SessionStart, SessionEnd; blocking + async hooks; Claude Code-compatible hooks.json format.

features.evidence_quote: Skills give OpenHands reusable instructions for specialized tasks. A skill can capture domain knowledge, define a repeatable workflow
features.note: Follows Agent Skills spec (SKILL.md); keyword triggers, path-triggered rules, org/user/global registries.

features.evidence_quote: Persistent memory lets an agent keep what it learned in plain Markdown files that are loaded back into the system prompt
features.note: Opt-in (load_memory=True); two-tier MEMORY.md (user ~/.openhands/memory/ + project workspace/.openhands/memory/); off by default.

features.evidence_quote: Docker sandbox (recommended) ... Runs the agent server inside a Docker container. Good isolation from your host machine.
features.note: Docker/process/remote providers; permission modes: always-ask (default), --always-approve, --llm-approve; SDK confirmation policies AlwaysConfirm/ConfirmRisky/NeverConfirm.

features.evidence_quote: a two-phase workflow where a custom planning agent (with read-only tools) analyzes tasks and creates structured plans
features.note: Plan-then-execute exists as a documented SDK pattern (planning agent writes PLAN.md, execution agent implements); CLI only has 'Plan - View agent plan'; no built-in interactive plan-approval gate in docs.

features.evidence_quote: Start running the conversation in the background.
features.note: Agent-server REST API runs conversations in background; bash commands also have a background start endpoint; Agent Canvas conversations run server-side.

features.evidence_quote: Use OpenHands directly in your favorite code editor through the Agent Client Protocol
features.note: ACP-based: Zed + JetBrains native support, VS Code via community ACP extension; marked experimental; GUI also embeds a VS Code tab.

features.evidence_quote: OpenHands can connect to any LLM supported by LiteLLM.
features.note: LiteLLM: Anthropic/OpenAI/Google/Azure/Bedrock/Groq/Moonshot/OpenRouter/local servers; also can drive Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI as ACP agents.

features.evidence_quote: Plugins bundle multiple agent components together—skills, hooks, MCP servers, agents, and commands—into reusable packages that extend OpenHands capabilities.
features.note: Claude Code plugin structure compatible (.claude-plugin/) plus portable Agent Plugins format with plugin.json at root.

features.evidence_quote: OpenHands CLI automatically saves your conversation history in ~/.openhands/conversations. You can resume any previous conversation to continue where you left off.
features.note: openhands --resume <id> / --resume --last; also works in ACP/IDE mode; automations' conversations can be continued too.

features.evidence_quote: The OpenHands SDK provides metrics tracking at two levels: individual LLM metrics and aggregated conversation-level costs
features.note: Token/cost/latency metrics per LLM and per conversation; Cloud org/user spending caps documented at https://docs.openhands.dev/openhands/usage/cloud/organizations/budgets.

result.promises: OpenHands Agent Canvas promises to turn your coding agents into a self-hosted, always-on engineering team — a developer control center for starting conversations and automating everyday tasks, run locally by default or across Docker, VM, and cloud backends with OpenHands, Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, or any ACP-compatible agent.
result.surprises: Repo All-Hands-AI/OpenHands now redirects to OpenHands/OpenHands and its v1.x release is 'Agent Canvas', a control center that can host third-party agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini) via ACP, while the OpenHands agent core moved to the separate software-agent-sdk and automation repos; hooks/skills formats are deliberately Claude Code-compatible.

features.evidence_quote: They allow you to delegate focused work to AI agents that are configured with task-specific prompts, tools, and behaviors.
features.note: Named subagents defined in Markdown+YAML; forking via subagent_type: "fork"; /agents manage; can continue finished agents with send_message.

features.evidence_quote: The leader creates a team, assigns up to three independent workstreams, and uses the existing team tools for messages and task state.
features.note: Experimental Agent Team runtime via /coordinate (shared task list, teammate messaging); also workflow scripts gated by tools.workflowsEnabled (/workflows lists runs), Agent Board cross-agent tasks, Arena multi-model competition, Herdr.

features.evidence_quote: Qwen Code can connect to external tools and data sources through the Model Context Protocol (MCP).
features.note: Client role; stdio, SSE, HTTP transports; servers manageable via /mcp and extensions. No MCP server mode found in docs.

features.evidence_quote: execute custom scripts or programs at specific points in the application lifecycle, such as before tool execution, after tool execution, at session start/end
features.note: Events include PreToolUse, PostToolUse, SessionStart, SessionEnd; configured in settings.json under hooks with matcher + executor; /hooks command manages them.

features.evidence_quote: Skills are stored as directories containing a `SKILL.md` file.
features.note: Model-invoked; personal ~/.qwen/skills/, project .qwen/skills/, bundled, extension-provided; auto-skill generation plus /curator maintenance; Agent Skills spec compatible.

features.evidence_quote: Two mechanisms carry knowledge across sessions so you don't have to re-explain yourself every time
features.note: QWEN.md/AGENTS.md instruction files plus auto-memory written by Qwen under ~/.qwen/projects/<project>/memory/ (Markdown files, managed with /dream, /forget).

features.evidence_quote: On Linux, install `bwrap` (Bubblewrap) for the strongest supported boundary, then enable the tool execution sandbox in your User settings
features.note: tools.executionSandbox backends bwrap/Landlock plus Docker/Podman/Seatbelt whole-CLI modes; filesystem workspace-write/read-only and network closed/open policies; five approval modes incl. classifier-based Auto.

features.evidence_quote: Plan Mode instructs Qwen Code to create a plan by analyzing the codebase with read-only operations
features.note: Distinct 'plan' approval mode (Shift+Tab cycle or /plan enter/exit), read-only, no edits or shell commands; proposes plan then user approves by switching modes.

features.evidence_quote: Top-level named subagents run in the background by default and deliver their results through completion notifications.
features.note: Also /tasks lists background tasks; /loop cron scheduled prompts (session-scoped); DashScope /batch-api async batch jobs; headless mode with --continue/--resume.

features.evidence_quote: The VS Code extension (Beta) lets you see Qwen's changes in real-time through a native graphical interface integrated directly into your IDE
features.note: VS Code extension (Beta), JetBrains via Agent Client Protocol, Zed integration; ACP session support with conversation history and context usage in-IDE.

features.evidence_quote: Qwen Code allows you to configure multiple model providers through the `modelProviders` setting in your `settings.json`.
features.note: Built-in auth types openai, anthropic, gemini, vertex-ai plus custom provider ids via providerProtocol; /model picker; Alibaba ModelStudio; OAuth models hard-coded.

features.evidence_quote: Qwen Code extensions package prompts, MCP servers, subagents, skills and custom commands into a familiar and user-friendly format.
features.note: qwen extensions CLI + /extensions manager with marketplace Discover tab; installs Gemini CLI Extensions Gallery, Claude Code Marketplace, and portable Agent Plugins v1 packages.

features.evidence_quote: Can resume previous sessions scoped to the current project for multi-step automation
features.note: Interactive /resume (alias /continue); CLI --continue and --resume <sessionId>; restored sessions re-add compatible background agents via list_agents.

features.evidence_quote: Use the `/stats` command to see your cached token savings
features.note: /stats shows cached token % and savings; /context detail breaks down resident prefix cost (tools, MCP, context files, skills); token caching automatic for API-key users. No hard spend limits documented.

result.promises: "The open-source AI coding agent for your terminal, editor, desktop, browser, and chat." It promises an agentic coding tool that lives in your terminal and turns ideas into code faster, spanning CLI, IDE, desktop, browser, and chat surfaces.
result.surprises: Ships built-in `claude-code` and `codex` subagent executors that delegate tasks to separately installed Claude Code (ACP) and Codex CLIs using their own models/auth, and it installs extensions directly from the Claude Code and Gemini CLI marketplaces.

features.evidence_quote: Boomerang Tasks (also known as subtasks or task orchestration) allow you to break down complex projects into smaller, manageable pieces
features.note: Built-in Orchestrator mode delegates via new_task tool; child task runs in isolated context, parent pauses and resumes with the child's summary. Subtask creation/completion auto-approvable.

features.evidence_quote: A strategic workflow orchestrator (aka Boomerang Mode) that breaks down complex tasks and delegates them to specialized modes.
features.note: Parent→child subtask chains with summary handoff only (sequential, no scripts/DAGs/swarms/YAML workflows). Worktrees allow parallel tasks in separate windows; message queueing sequences input.

features.evidence_quote: Model Context Protocol (MCP) extends Roo Code's capabilities by connecting to external tools and services.
features.note: MCP client with stdio/SSE/streamable-HTTP transports, global mcp_settings.json + project .roo/mcp.json, per-tool auto-approve, marketplace install. No evidence Roo itself acts as an MCP server.

No lifecycle-hook feature (pre/post tool, session start/stop) found in any docs page or in the repo source (no hook files/config keys). Nearest extension points are MCP tools, custom modes, and experimental custom tools; nothing documented either way.

features.evidence_quote: Skills package task-specific instructions that Roo loads on-demand when your request matches the skill's purpose.
features.note: SKILL.md with progressive disclosure; ~/.roo/skills and .roo/skills (also cross-agent ~/.agents/skills), mode targeting, bundled scripts/templates, project overrides global.

features.evidence_quote: A separate Git repository created specifically for checkpoint tracking that functions as the persistent storage mechanism for checkpoint state.
features.note: No memory-bank/long-term memory feature. Persistence comes from shadow-git checkpoints, resumable task history (conversations stored and reopened), and file-based rules (.roorules / AGENTS.md loaded each session).

features.evidence_quote: Auto-approve settings bypass confirmation prompts, giving Roo direct access to your system.
features.note: Permission modes exist: per-action auto-approve tiles (read/edit/commands/MCP/browser/mode-switch), command whitelisting, CLI --require-approval. No OS-level sandbox — rooignore docs state '.rooignore ... does not create a system-level sandbox.'

features.evidence_quote: An experienced technical leader and planner who helps design systems and create implementation plans
features.note: Architect mode is a dedicated planning persona restricted to markdown-only edits. No formal plan-then-approve gate; the user approves implicitly by switching to Code/Debug mode.

features.evidence_quote: Supports long-running commands that continue in the background
features.note: Long-running terminal commands keep running, later checked via read_command_output; message queueing and the headless CLI (--print/--oneshot) are async-ish. No managed background-task queue for agent tasks.

features.evidence_quote: Roo Code is a VS Code extension that brings AI-powered coding assistance directly to your editor.
features.note: VS Code Marketplace + Open VSX; works in Cursor, VSCodium, Windsurf. No JetBrains plugin. CLI also ships (apps/cli, npm-free shell installer) for terminal use.

features.evidence_quote: Roo is model-agnostic, allowing you to choose the model that best fits your needs
features.note: Docs list ~28 providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, Bedrock, Vertex, OpenRouter, xAI, Mistral, DeepSeek, Z.ai, Ollama, LM Studio, OpenAI-compatible, etc.); per-mode sticky model selection; API configuration profiles.

features.evidence_quote: The Roo Code Marketplace is a central hub for discovering and installing extensions, known as MCPs (Model Context Protocol) and Modes.
features.note: Third-party distribution via marketplace (MCP servers + custom modes) and experimental defineCustomTool TS/JS tool API. No formal plugin/extension API with lifecycle or packaging spec beyond this.

features.evidence_quote: When you resume a task from history, it uses the same profile it had originally
features.note: Task history persists conversations and tasks can be reopened/resumed (resumeTask+isTaskInHistory also in the extension API); CLI supports session/task IDs (--create-with-session-id, taskId in stdin stream mode).

features.evidence_quote: Roo Code automatically calculates the estimated cost of each API request based on the configured model's pricing.
features.note: Per-request input/output token counts and estimated cost shown in chat (incl. reasoning tokens); 'Max Requests' cap for auto-approved actions forces re-approval; per-profile rate limits; supports free local models.

result.promises: Roo Code promises "Your AI-Powered Dev Team, Right in Your Editor" — a whole team of AI agents inside VS Code that generate code from natural language, adapt with Code/Architect/Ask/Debug and custom modes, refactor and debug existing code, write documentation, answer codebase questions, automate repetitive tasks, and plug into external tools via MCP.
result.surprises: The project is discontinued: the README states the extension "was shut down on May 15th" (2026) — the same date as the final v3.54.0 release — and redirects users to the community fork ZooCode or to Cline.
